en: a. needing someone or something else for support or to survive; determined by something else; n. a person who relies on another for financial support
ex: Young children are completely dependent on their parents.
年幼的孩子完全依賴父母。

en: vt. to have earned or be worthy of something because of your actions or qualities; vi. to be worthy of reward or punishment
ex: She worked hard and deserves a promotion.
她很努力，應該得到升遷。

en: prep. without being affected by something; in spite of; n. an angry feeling towards someone
ex: We went out despite the rain.
儘管下雨，我們還是出門了。

en: n. the act of destroying something completely; the state of being destroyed; the cause of destroying something
ex: The war caused widespread destruction in the city.
戰爭在這座城市造成廣泛的破壞。

en: n. a machine or tool that is made for a particular purpose; a plan or trick used to get something; a design or pattern used for decoration; a bomb
ex: This device can record and play videos.
這個裝置可以錄影和播放影片。

en: vt. to invent or plan something such as a method or system; to leave land or property to someone in a will; n. a gift of property by will
ex: The engineers devised a new way of cleaning the water.
工程師想出了新的淨水方法。

en: vt. to give a lot of your time, energy or attention to something; to give yourself completely to a person or a cause; to set apart for a special purpose
ex: She devoted her life to helping the poor.
她把一生都奉獻給幫助窮人。

en: vt. to break down food in the stomach so that the body can use it; to understand and remember new information; vi. (of food) to be broken down in the stomach; n. a short summary of a book, report or article
ex: It takes a few hours to digest a big meal.
消化一頓大餐需要好幾個小時。

en: n. careful and persistent effort in your work or duties
ex: Her diligence in studying earned her a scholarship.
她用功讀書，因此獲得獎學金。

en: n. an event that causes great damage, loss or suffering; a complete failure; an extremely bad situation
ex: The earthquake was a terrible natural disaster.
那場地震是一場可怕的天災。

en: vt. to make someone lose confidence or enthusiasm; to try to prevent someone from doing something by showing disapproval; to make something less likely to happen
ex: Don't let one failure discourage you from trying again.
別讓一次失敗使你不敢再試。

en: n. clothing or a manner used to hide who you are; an artificial manner used to hide your feelings; vt. to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you; to hide the truth about something
ex: The spy entered the building in disguise.
間諜喬裝潛入那棟大樓。

en: n. a feeling of strong dislike or disapproval; a feeling that makes you want to be sick; vt. to make someone feel very unpleasant or sick; vi. to cause such a feeling
ex: She turned away in disgust at the sight of the rotten food.
她看到腐爛的食物，厭惡地轉過頭去。

en: a. clearly noticeable; separate and different from something else; (of a sound, image or idea) easy to see, hear or understand
ex: There is a distinct difference between the two products.
這兩項產品有明顯的差異。

en: a. very successful and respected; having an important place in a group or society; (of appearance) elegant and dignified
ex: He is a distinguished professor at the university.
他是這所大學的傑出教授。

en: n. the act of giving something out to a number of people; the way in which something is spread over an area; the process of delivering goods to shops
ex: The distribution of food to the refugees began this morning.
給難民的食物分發今天早上開始了。

en: n. an area of a country, city or town with particular features; a part of a country or city that is officially separated; an area used as an official unit
ex: They live in a quiet residential district.
他們住在安靜的住宅區。

en: a. made up of many different types of people or things; very different from each other
ex: The city has a diverse population from many countries.
這座城市有來自許多國家的多元人口。

en: a. relating to God or a god; wonderful or perfect; n. a priest or theologian; vt. to discover something by guessing or intuition
ex: Many people believe in divine power.
許多人相信神的力量。
ph: to err is human, to forgive divine
犯錯乃人之常情，寬恕乃神性

en: n. the legal end of a marriage; a complete separation between two things; vt. to legally end a marriage with someone; to separate something completely from something else
ex: They got a divorce after ten years of marriage.
他們結婚十年後離婚了。

en: a. more important, strong or noticeable than others; having the most influence or control; (in genetics) a gene that shows its effect
ex: The company holds a dominant position in the market.
該公司在市場上占主導地位。

en: vi. to be carried slowly along by water or air; to move slowly without a clear purpose; to gradually change from one condition to another; n. a slow movement; the general meaning of something; a pile of something blown by wind
ex: The boat drifted slowly down the river.
船順著河流緩緩漂流而下。

en: a. able to last a long time without being damaged or broken; strong and not easily worn out; long-lasting
ex: These boots are very durable and last for years.
這雙靴子非常耐用，可以穿好幾年。

en: a. serious and sincere; showing strong feelings and a desire to do something well; n. a sum of money paid as a guarantee; a serious state of mind
ex: He made an earnest effort to improve his grades.
他認真地努力提高成績。

en: a. not wasting money, time or other resources; costing little to use; cheap and good value
ex: This car is very economical because it uses little fuel.
這輛車很省油，非常經濟實惠。

en: n. the study of how money, goods and services are produced and used in a society; the financial aspects of something
ex: He is studying economics at a university.
他在大學主修經濟學。

en: n. an expert in economics; a person who studies or writes about how economies work
ex: The economist predicted that prices would rise next year.
經濟學家預測明年物價將上漲。

en: a. able to stretch and return to the original shape; able to change to suit new conditions; (of a regulation) not strict; n. a material that can stretch and return to its shape
ex: The skirt has an elastic waistband for comfort.
這條裙子有彈性腰帶，穿起來舒服。

en: a. dealing with the most basic parts of a subject; easy and not difficult; relating to the earliest stage of education
ex: He teaches elementary school math.
他教小學數學。

en: vt. to make people obey a rule or law; to make something happen by using force or authority; to put pressure on someone to do something; (enforcement) the act of making sure that a law is obeyed
ex: The police enforce the traffic laws strictly.
警方嚴格執行交通法規。

en: vt. to make something bigger; to make a photograph bigger; to describe something in more detail; vi. to become bigger; (enlargement) the act of making something larger; a larger copy of a photograph
ex: They plan to enlarge the kitchen next year.
他們計畫明年擴建廚房。

en: a. extremely large in size, amount or degree; much more than usual
ex: The company made an enormous profit last year.
公司去年賺了一大筆利潤。

en: vt. to amuse people by performing; to welcome guests and give them food and drink; to consider an idea or possibility; vi. to give guests food and drink; (entertainment) things such as films and shows that amuse people
ex: The magician entertained the children with card tricks.
魔術師用紙牌戲法逗樂了孩子們。

en: n. the state of being equal, especially in rights, status and opportunities; the quality of being the same in size, amount or value; (in math) the state of being equal
ex: The group fights for gender equality in the workplace.
這個團體為職場的性別平等而努力。

en: vt. to provide someone or something with the things they need for a particular purpose; to prepare someone for something; (equipment) the tools or machines needed for a particular job
ex: The hospital was equipped with modern medical equipment.
醫院配備了現代化的醫療設備。

en: vt. to start a company, organization or system that is likely to last for a long time; to show that something is true; to make something accepted; vi. (of a plant) to take root; (establishment) an organization or business
ex: The school was established in 1900.
這所學校創立於 1900 年。

en: vt. to judge the value or quality of something; to calculate the amount or value of something; to test someone's knowledge or performance
ex: We need to evaluate the results of the experiment.
我們需要評估實驗的結果。

en: n. facts or signs that show that something is true; information used in a court of law to prove something; a sign or clear indication of something; vt. to show or prove something
ex: The police found no evidence of a crime.
警方沒有發現犯罪的證據。

en: n. something that is not included in a general rule or statement; a case in which a rule does not apply; an objection or complaint about something
ex: Everyone must attend, with no exceptions.
每個人都必須出席，無一例外。

en: vt. to make someone very tired; to use up all of something; to try every possible way to do something; n. the waste gas that comes out of a vehicle's engine; a pipe through which the waste gas passes
ex: The long hike exhausted all of us.
長途健行讓我們都筋疲力盡。
